To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction of benzylidenedioxindoles with 1,4-diketones in the presence of Sc(OTF)3 in reflux of hexane afforded the corresponding products with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities.

the reaction of benzylidenedioxindole and tetralin in refluxing hexanes with catalytic amount of Lewis acids such as Sc(OTf)(3) and Yb(OTf)(2) gave tetralin-fuse spiroindoline with excellent diastereo- and regioselectivities.
the reaction of benzylidenedioxindoles with Sc(OTf3)3 in reflux hexane affords highly diastereomerically enriched tetralin-fusedsiprooxindoles in good chemical yields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the synthesis of tetraline-fused spiroindoline derivatives, which is based on a Lewis-acid catalysed C(sp3)-H bond functionalisation reaction.
the Lewis acid-catalyzed functionalization of C(sp3)-H bonds, which is a new and highly effective approach for constructing spirocyclic compounds.
the development of a highly diastereospecific synthesis of tetraline-fused spiro[oxindole-indole] derivatives by means of Lewis acid-catalyzed direct C(sp3)-H functionalization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Lewis acid catalyzed C(sp 3)–H bond functionalization of benzylidenedioxindole derivatives with 2,2,2-trichloroacetamide is a highly diastereospecific reaction that proceeds through the intermediacy of a 2,2-dichloro-2,3-dihydro-1,3-benzoxazolone species.

the reaction is initiated by Lewis acid-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization of the enamine intermediate to generate the spirocyclic product and the subsequent interconversion between the two diastereo-meric products is driven by their different solubility in the reaction mixture.

this reaction mechanism is a complex one and it involves several factors, including the formation of the intermediate 3 (Scheme 2) by C–H activation of the substrate, the interconversion of the diastereomeric intermediate 3, and the solubility difference of the two diasteromers in the reaction system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reaction of benzylidenedioxindoles with Sc(OTf3)3 as the Lewis acid catalyst is a highly diastereospecific C–H functionalization of the benzylic C(sp3) bond.
this reaction could be regarded as a rare example of Lewis-acid-catalyzed highly diastereospecific C(sp3)−H bond functionalization.
this method is highly efficient for the synthesis of tetralins and spirooxindoles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Lewis acid can catalyze a diastereoselection reaction of a C(sp3) – H bond in a spirocyclic system.
